newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea physical crude markets subdued, paper steady.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea physical crude markets subdued, paper steady.

text.p: North Sea crude markets saw little physical activity on Thursday while Brent paper spreads held steady as outright prices made modest gains.
"It's as dead as a dodo," said one physical trader.
The only wet deal reported was a Flotta loading Jan 5-7 which changed hands at Dated Brent -35 cents.
Three Forties cargoes, a Statfjord and an Oseberg traded on Wednesday, all at levels broadly steady on previous deals.
"Today I'd say differentials are basically unchanged from yesterday but it's hard to get a handle on things when nothing actually moves," said one dealer.
All three Brent cargoes set to turn wet on Thursday were still on the move through the paper chains ahead of the five o'clock deadline, traders said.
Dated Brent was pegged around Jan Brent +30 cents, having traded twice at Jan +33 cents on Wednesday, with a third cargo thought to have traded at +23 cents, although this was not confirmed.
On the paper markets, Jan Brent traded twice at $22.65 and twice at $22.50, the level at which it was talked at 1630 GMT.
The Jan/Feb spread traded steady at +47 and +48 cents, and was discussed at +43/48 cents later. Feb/March talked at +50/53.
Next week's CFDs were talked at Jan Brent -13/-9 cents. Jan 13-17 was traded against Jan 27-31 at +25 cents.
